bottleneck: Not a throughput lever: this trial pins the applicability of the Controller's real BF16 C128 decode trace to this candidate tree. The trace (a1, commit 15fd7f4, 16 forwards, 8560 kernels) reports step[DECODE bs=128] with exactly one cudaGraphLaunch inside every one of its 16 host step spans, 28 attention launches per forward with one constant grid (159,1,2), and 16 lm_head launches. KV byte accounting at the engine's own label (M=128, seq 513-576, 2048 B/token/layer) gives 225.8-253.5 GB/s attention (82.7-92.9% of the 273 GB/s peak) and is the only M coherent with the same step's GEMM (199 GB/s) and lm_head (214 GB/s); M=64 is numerically feasible (113-127 GB/s) so the control is not rigged, and M=256 is impossible (452-507 GB/s). However, the recorded launch passes --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64, and in this tree that flag resolves to decode.max_bs=64, the AST-executed capture-list generator tops out at 64 (128 excluded; max_bs=256 control includes it), and DecodeCudaGraphRunner.can_run_graph replays only when batch_size <= max_bs under the default padding path. So this tree cannot execute the observed 128-row graph replay under the recorded argv: the profiled tree's resolved decode-graph configuration differs from HEAD's.

learning: Executed facts. (a) The real C128 trace is one unsplit 128-row forward per step (16 spans, 16 cudaGraphLaunch, exactly one per span; 28 attention launches per forward with a single constant grid (159,1,2); 16 lm_head launches), and its KV byte model closes only at M=128 (225.8-253.5 GB/s, 82.7-92.9% of peak) versus an M=64 control that is feasible but would leave attention at 41-46% of peak while every other kernel in the same step runs at 73-79%. (b) In this candidate tree the recorded --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 cannot produce that replay: the real capture-list generator executed with max_bs=64 tops out at 64, memory_hook materializes decode.bs from decode.max_bs, and DecodeCudaGraphRunner replays only when batch_size <= max_bs (padding enabled). The sensitivity control (max_bs=256 includes 128) shows the check is not a constant. (c) Therefore the profiled run's resolved decode-graph config is not HEAD's: either its arg resolution differed at commit 15fd7f4 or an unrecorded mechanism expanded capture. The trace remains a valid M=128 bandwidth observation but is NOT evidence about HEAD's C128/C256 graph coverage, and t15's 'eager at bs>64' alternative for the C256 gap loses its support. Limits: run-tree source is unavailable (15fd7f4 is not an object in this repo), step labels are host arguments not device occupancy (the packet's own trace_validation says so), record_shapes=false means M=128 is inferred from the label plus per-class bandwidth coherence rather than read from tensor shapes, and seq is bounded from the 512+<=64 workload rather than measured. No speed, numeric, quality, Candidate, Promotion or best_verified claim; F3 remains UNGATED and untouched.
